required_changes: F1: guard the post-callback backend call in Canvas.close (both branches).
F2: make create_native a no-op on a closed canvas.

Control A (CPU, real offscreen PyQt6): Canvas.close() whose close handler calls sip.delete(parent); assert no exception, one close event, one destroy, _backend is None; add a raising-handler variant asserting the original error propagates with no cleanup-failed log.

Control B (CPU real Qt, plus one GPU case with a live shared peer): explicit Canvas.close() then parent deletion; assert one close event, peer still renders, gauges zero; this is the only native check of the double destroy_canvas(id).
Control C: create_native() and a late update() after destruction are no-ops.
Before any PyQt5/PySide6 claim: run the parent-deletion and Control A cases under each binding; otherwise state PyQt6-only scope in the manifests.
Re-run the CPU suite and the Windows/WSL overlays on the new hashes; 647/648/650 do not cover the changed canvas.py.
scope: Independent read-only two-runtime-file/CPU-GPU evidence review; no packaging or release approval.
reviewer_limits: Read-only: nothing executed, no hashes recomputed, F1/F2 derived by code trace and not reproduced.
runtime.patch is a whole-file rewrite; the changed regions were reviewed in current source, not byte-diffed against frozen.
Native destroy_canvas idempotence and id reuse were not inspected (no native source found under src/); the double-release tolerance is assumed from existing behaviour.
PyQt5 and PySide6 behaviour is unverified; conclusions about them are by reasoning only.
Deleting a widget from inside its own closeEvent or paintEvent is Qt-level undefined behaviour and was not assessed.

The _qt.py BSD header is present in the patch; the canvas.py header, LICENSE and LICENSE-BSD contents were not read. test_window_state_cpu.py, test_layout_reparent_gpu.py, junit files and run 649 were not read.
No approval is given for packaging, installed-wheel qualification, native WSI, Metal, physical Linux GPU or VisPy parity.
